senses.gloss: אָנְקְלַי f. (אנק, with ל format.; = אוּנְקַי; corresp. to b. h. לוּלַי; Greek adapt. ἀγκολη, LXX Ex. XXVI, 10; cmp. אוֹנִי as to contact of the two languages) prop. little (camel’s) neck, hence

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 12:2">Kel. XII, 2</cite> <he>א׳ של כתפין</he> Ar. (ed. <he>אונקליות</he>, <he>אונקלין</he> with adject. in the sing., corr. acc.) the carriers’ hook attached to their yoke, pole &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 12:2">Ib.</cite> <he>א׳ של דרגש</he> the hook of the bedstead (used for fastening the girths to the posts); <he>של נקליטין</he> the rack of the bed-curtain, v. <cite ref="N01224"><he>נַקְלִיטִין</he></cite>. Ib. 3 <he>א׳ שבכותלים</he> hook attached to walls.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Tevul Yom 4:6">T’bul Yom IV, 6</cite> <he>ואנ׳ שלהם קיימת</he> and the hook (attached to the now broken yoke) remained unimpaired; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="A00771"><he>אוּנְקְלָאוֹת</he></cite>, <he>אָנְקְ׳</he>, (<he>אונקלין</he>) <he>אוּנְקְלִיּוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Tamid 3:5">Tam. III, 5</cite>; Mid. III, 5; a. fr.—Kel. l. c.; <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 2:4">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. II, 4</cite>; v. <cite ref="A00764"><he>אוּנְקַי</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: [cmp. ἀγκαλίς in S.] the load carried on the hook, the farmer’s load of sheaves or bunches; cmp. בלונקי.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 4:10">Tosef. Maas. Sh. IV, 10</cite>. <he>כל הא׳</he> the whole load. [<cite ref="Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 4:11">Ib. 11</cite> <cite ref="A00762"><he>אונקולין</he></cite>, <cite ref="A00775"><he>אונקלי</he></cite>, read with ed. Zuck. <he>אינפולי</he>].

senses.gloss: Trnsf. (medic.) bent cartilage, esp. the cartilage (cart. ensiformis) at the end of the sternum which, being bent inside, presses on the stomach and creates nausea &c.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 29a:4">Ab. Zar. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>מעלין א׳ וכ׳</he> you are permitted to lift the cartilage on the Sabbath (by means of a bandage &c.).
Ib. מאי א׳ וכ׳ what unklay is meant? Ans. the cartilage in front of the heart; v. אִיסְתּוֹמְכָא.
